A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AffectGPT, MER-Caption, and MER-UniBench research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison despite reformatting and the addition of Appendix N.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, dataset and model ablations, preliminary description-generation experiments, and an annotation-quality user study in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds encoder, LoRA-rank, and frame-sampling experiments in Figure 4, Table 8, and Appendix N.

M1.justification: The annotation pipeline, Q-Former and attention pre-fusion alternatives, training objective, and inference framework remain unchanged. Newly stated defaults and the clarified model-selection rationale document existing choices; the added component experiments do not establish a revised proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same training datasets and nine MER-UniBench datasets covering fine-grained emotion recognition, basic emotion recognition, and sentiment analysis. Appendix J clarifies the single-person scope without changing the represented datasets or samples. Encoder and frame-count sweeps do not add task coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Table 2, the complete appendix benchmark results, and the preliminary description-generation comparison. The new encoder substitutions and LoRA variants are internal ablations, not newly evaluated competing emotion-understanding methods.

E3.justification: v2 adds configuration sweeps over audio/video encoders, LoRA removal and ranks 8/16/32, and 2–64 sampled frames under face-only and face-text inputs, including a text-only control. Existing dataset splits, metrics, training budgets, and the 20-sample, four-expert user-study design remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The analysis substantially expands beyond the retained filtering, pre-fusion, input-modality, and LLM ablations. Figure 4(b,c) tests encoder dependence, Table 8 isolates LoRA's contribution and rank sensitivity, and Appendix N/Figure 10 tests temporal sampling sensitivity under two input combinations.

E5.justification: The existing ± reporting in the preliminary experiments is unchanged between v1 Table 9 and v2 Table 10. v2 adds no run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or statistical-testing procedures; the new ablations report point estimates.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial result sets concerning encoder dependence, LoRA benefits, and frame-sampling sensitivity. For example, Table 8 reports 73.30 without LoRA, 74.77 at rank 16, and 74.92 at rank 32. These are new configuration comparisons; the original main and appendix benchmark scores, including AffectGPT's 74.77 mean, remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The training objective, fusion equations, grouping functions, and evaluation definitions in Equations 1–13 remain unchanged. Added explanations of fusion efficiency and metric motivation introduce no new formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same dataset, pre-fusion model, and unified benchmark contributions, including the largest descriptive-dataset claim and the reported improvement of over 9% against existing MLLMs. Additional experiments support these retained claims.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands qualifications and interpretation. Section 4 discusses the inability to assess additional incorrect emotion labels without finer reference annotations; Section 5 acknowledges remaining MER-Caption+ annotation errors; Appendix J explicitly limits coverage to single-person videos. New discussion also interprets filtering weaknesses, encoder differences, LoRA tradeoffs, and frame-sampling saturation.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies default LoRA rank 16 and eight sampled frames, explains instruction-data filtering through emotion extraction and removal of empty outputs, and clarifies individual-model selection in Appendix F. It also supplies an explicit public repository link and release statement, replacing the supplementary-code reference. These are documentation and access changes, not established revisions to existing settings.

R1.justification: The cultural-emotion citation changes from Mesquita and Leu to Matsumoto, the MLLM survey citation changes from Yin et al. to Liang et al., and the AdamW reference is removed. The principal related-work discussion and novelty positioning remain intact; several other reference changes merely update publication metadata.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized copyedits and explanatory expansions, separates the dataset-effectiveness discussion from its filtering ablation, and adds acknowledgments and Appendix N. Affiliations and citation style also change. The main section sequence and most existing prose remain recognizable.

P2.justification: The main text changes from a single-column layout to an ICML two-column layout, extensively resizing and relocating figures and tables. Figure 4 expands into three panels, Table 8 and Figure 10 are added, and the benchmark-statistics table gains a Data Source column. Most other displays retain their underlying content.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens validation through encoder, LoRA, and frame-sampling controls and improves reproducibility through clearer defaults, filtering details, and code-access information. Its explicit metric and annotation limitations improve interpretability. The gains are incremental: the core results remain unchanged, and the acknowledged limitations and sparse uncertainty reporting remain unresolved.
